_comment: Curated root causes for scripts/campfire-suite. Unpassed tests are clustered
mechanically by failure message; this file is what turns a cluster into a
named todo with an owner. Rules are tried in order; FIRST MATCH WINS, so the
specific ones sit above the general ones.
`match` keys on the failure MESSAGE. A rule may add `match_test`, keyed on the
test identifier, and then both have to hold — which is the only way to name a
SILENT divergence, since every wrong answer reads as the same assertion failure.
The unit is an UNPASSED TEST, not a FAIL line: a file that dies at load
contributes its whole count against its load error. See the header of
scripts/campfire-suite-summary.
Counts churn — 130 unpassed is a shadow. Causes are the worklist, so they
carry stable slugs you can still discuss forty commits later.
owner:
compiler — roundhouse modeling debt. Ours to fix.
app      — a campfire idiom that could change upstream. Only ever a
plain-Rails change that stands on its own merits under stock
Rails; the port never asks for app-side divergence.
gem      — a gem whose surface we shim, or one deliberately out of scope.
spinel   — upstream spinel.
harness  — this harness's own gap, not the emit's.
subset   — the test reaches for dynamic Ruby no compiled target has
(a per-object `extend`, `define_method`, `eval`). Nobody
can act: not a todo, named so it is not triaged twice, and
left out of the who-can-act line.
unknown  — the cluster is real, its root cause is not yet known.
THE TAIL IS FLAT. Nothing here blocks more than a handful of tests, and the
clusters are shapes of wall rather than single fixes — following ONE test
down its chain has repeatedly beaten ranking the clusters, because a fix
usually exposes the next wall rather than greening a file. Read the ranking
as a map of what KINDS of thing are missing, not as a queue.

A rule matching zero tests is reported too, in one of three ways: cleared (it carries `at_zero` saying so, and stays as a regression tripwire), held at zero by a stub (`stubbed`), or unexplained — which means the cause may be cleared, or its message may have moved and the count is now quietly understating.

causes.title: The emitted test base class is missing Rails' test surface
causes.match: undefined method '(file_fixture|fixture_file_upload|assert[a-z_]*|response|parsed_body)' for an instance of \S*Test\b
causes.note: Not the app's code failing — the scaffolding around it. `file_fixture` and `fixture_file_upload` read from test/fixtures/files, `response` is the integration-test response object, and the bare `assert` family comes from Minitest itself. Every one of these is a method the emitted TestBase would have to answer before the assertion behind it is even reached, so this cluster hides an unknown number of further walls.
causes.at_zero: the family landed over several commits, `fixture_file_upload` last in f86ac0b6; the rule stays as a regression tripwire.

causes.title: A link-preview attachment node is served bare, not rendered through `_opengraph_embed`
causes.note: Rails renders every `` in a stored body through the attachable's partial before serving it, and only then hands the body to `auto_link`, whose default-list sanitize strips the outer tag but keeps the rendered children. `Content#to_s` now does that for sgid attachables — an @mention reaches the page as `users/_mention` on both lanes (it used to be served as nothing: the ruby lane's `auto_link` stripped the bare tag with nothing inside, spinel's served an element a browser draws as nothing) — through the generated `Content.render_attachment`, one arm per attachable model naming a partial. A link preview is the OTHER dispatch in campfire's `from_node` reopen: not an sgid but the content-type `application/vnd.actiontext.opengraph-embed`, built by `OpengraphEmbed.from_node` with `web_url` dropping a non-web `href`/`url` (these tests: `javascript:`, `data:`, this Campfire's own host), rendered through `action_text/attachables/_opengraph_embed` where `Free cookies` is the filename and the `` its image. That arm is not generated yet, and the emitted partial is not callable as emitted: Rails names its local after `model_name.element` (`opengraph_embed`), the view lowering named it after the directory (`attachable`), and `caption` reads through the Attachment's delegation to the node. Both lanes' sanitizers DO drop the `javascript:` href (verified on each lane's filter-chain output) — `data:image/svg` survives only because `web_url` never ran.

causes.title: A test-local helper with keyword defaults, called with a subset of its keywords
causes.match: (URI should be a String, Regexp, Addressable::Template, a callable object, or respond to #to_str\. Got: Hash|unexpected end of input)
causes.note: `def stub_successful_request(url: "https://www.example.com/", title: "Hey!", description: "desc..")` called as `stub_successful_request title: "…", description: "…"`: the caller's keywords arrive as one Hash in the first positional slot, so `url` IS the hash and WebMock (ruby) refuses it while the compiled lane stubs nothing and the controller answers an empty body (`unexpected end of input` from the test's `JSON.parse`). The other callers pass no keywords and take every default, which is why the helper worked until 977cbcd added this test. Keyword parameters with defaults on a test-module method need the same call-site fill-in the app-side lowering does.

causes.title: Active Storage's direct-upload controllers are not mounted, so their guard cannot be asserted
causes.match: (active_storage_authentication_test\.rb:|undefined method 'rails_direct_uploads_path'|uninitialized constant ActiveStorage::Current|undefined method 'count' for class ActiveStorage::Blob)
causes.note: Upstream 79eb9a5 (#267) requires a Campfire session on `ActiveStorage::DirectUploadsController` and the disk service's PUT — framework controllers campfire never calls (it uploads through MessagesController) but which Rails mounts on every app. The four tests drive those routes (`rails_direct_uploads_path`, `ActiveStorage::Blob.count`, `ActiveStorage::Current`) and expect 401 for an anonymous caller and 200 for a signed-in one. This emit mounts neither endpoint, so an anonymous caller gets a 404 rather than a 401: guarded by absence, which satisfies the intent and fails the assertion. DEFERRED rather than declined — serving the direct-upload endpoints only to guard them is not a feature anyone asked for, and the honest fix, if the routes ever land, is to land the guard with them. On spinel the file does not link (`Blob.count` on a class the runtime types differently), so all four count against the build.

causes.title: mocha's `.raises` on a class-method stub
causes.note: `ActionCable.server.stubs(:remote_connections).raises(RuntimeError.new("cable down"))` (upstream 9dd19d0's sessions test): the MochaBridge shapes answer `stubs(...).returns(v)` on a served row or a class; `.raises(e)` is the same slot with a raise in the arm, not a value. Spinel lane only; CRuby replays through the bridge.

causes.title: mocha's bare `mock` — an anonymous expectation object
causes.note: `mock` with no receiver builds an anonymous Mocha::Mock the test then hands to the code under test (upstream 9dd19d0's sessions test: `remote_connections = mock; remote_connections.expects(:disconnect).with(reconnect: true)`, then a second `mock.tap { |m| m.expects(:where)… }` returned from `ActionCable.server.stubs(:remote_connections)`). The MochaBridge shapes cover `stubs`/`expects` on an existing object and on a class; a free-standing mock is a new shape — an object whose whole interface is the expectations set on it. Spinel lane only; CRuby replays through the bridge.

causes.title: A user `call` with more required params than a poly `.call` site supplies drops the site's Proc arm — spinel#4529
causes.match: (undefined method 'call' for an instance of Proc|assert_difference failed: expected -2, got 0)
causes.note: All four passed on campfire 94a48aac and went red on 977cbcd in files upstream did not touch. Bisected on the emitted tree: the trigger is the new `LogScrubbingFormatter < Logger::Formatter` (upstream ef147d1, bot-key log redaction) and its one method, `call(severity, time, progname, message)`. spinel's pure-callable fast path for a poly `.call` steps aside whenever ANY user class defines `call`, expecting the poly method dispatch to carry the callable pre-arm (#4395) — but the dispatch counts a user `call` as a candidate only when `argc >= nrequired`, and with none it declines to the unresolved raise. A four-parameter `call` beside a two-argument `pred.call(host, port)` on the TcpSocketStub/Resolv seam lands exactly between the two guards, so the site compiles to an unconditional NoMethodError with no arm at all. `Room::PushTest#test_destroys_invalid_subscriptions` fails downstream of the same lost call (the endpoint resolver's Proc). Standalone 25-line repro and the arity discriminator (2 params passes; 3, 4, 5 fail) in the issue; the fix makes the fast path's guard arity-aware, the dispatch's own rule, and all four pass on the patched compiler (39/39 across the three files).
causes.at_zero: spinel#4529 closed by PR #4530 (b93306b6, same day): the fast path's guard is arity-aware; spinel lane 286 -> 290/300 on the merge. The rule stays as the tripwire for the two guards disagreeing again.

causes.title: A fixture accessor the emitted loader never defined
causes.match: undefined method '\w+' for an instance of \S*Test\b
causes.note: `users(:david)`-style accessors are generated per fixture file. Where one is missing the test cannot name its own data, so nothing behind it has been seen. The name comes from the app's own fixtures rather than from Rails, which is what separates this from the emitted test base class's own surface.

causes.title: `becomes!` — recasting a record to an STI sibling
causes.match: undefined method 'becomes!' for an instance of
causes.note: campfire opens and closes rooms by recasting: `room.becomes!(Rooms::Open)` rewrites the type column and returns the record as the sibling class. The STI read and write halves landed first (7aad7ba7, 7245435a); the recast followed in f2d42854, where the copy went into the LOWERER.
causes.at_zero: `becomes!` landed in f2d42854; the rule stays as a regression tripwire.

causes.title: A params object read as a Hash
causes.match: (for an instance of \w*Params\b|undefined method 'to_attrs' for an instance of Hash|method 'require' called for an instance of Hash)
causes.note: The emit gives each permitted set its own type (`RoomParams`), and the app then indexes it, deletes from it, or hands it somewhere expecting a Hash. Both directions are the same modeling question — what a params object IS — and it is the one the indifferent-access design addresses.

causes.title: A relation answering as an Array, or an Array asked for relation methods
causes.note: Both directions of one gap: a query lowered to an Array is then asked for `find_by`/`new`/a dynamic finder, or a Relation is asked for an Enumerable method the shim does not carry. `Model.where(...)` is a relation, not an array of records (eb57882f) — this is the residue of that same distinction.

causes.title: `ActionText::Attachment.from_node` — building an attachment from a parsed node
causes.note: Was named in docs/pipeline/runtime.md's "What is left" for attachments, alongside `ActionText::Attachables::MissingAttachable`. The PARSE already worked — `#attachments` returns every node with every attribute it carried — so this is the constructor that turns one of those nodes back into an attachment object, plus the missing-attachable case a stale sgid should land in.
causes.at_zero: `from_node`, `#attachable` and `MissingAttachable` landed with the generated `ActionText::Attachable.locate` (the includer set is the registry); the rule stays as a regression tripwire.

causes.title: An sgid minted by Rails, read here — campfire's tolerant `from_node` for a rotated secret
causes.note: campfire's `lib/rails_ext/action_text_attachables.rb` reopens `ActionText::Attachment.from_node` to accept a `User` sgid whose SIGNATURE fails, so rotating SECRET_KEY_BASE does not orphan every @mention: it decodes Rails' `_rails.data` base64 envelope by hand and finds the record from the gid inside. Two things stood between that and this runtime: the wire format (`SignedGlobalId` signed `<Model>/<id>` under its own salt, so an sgid a real Rails minted — every @mention in an existing database — read as missing, and the reopen's `_rails.data` read found no gid in ours), and the reopen itself, an `ActiveSupport.on_load` block the class finder skipped without a word. Both closed: the mint is Rails' bytes (`gid://<app>/<Model>/<id>?expires_in` as `data`, url-safe padded base64, HMAC-SHA1 under `signed_global_ids` — measured against Rails 8.2 and pinned as a literal in runtime/ruby/test/action_text_test.rb), and `ingest::on_load_reopen` reads the reopen for the one fact it holds, the `%w[ User ]` list, which `Attachment#attachable` consults through `SignedGlobalId.unverified_uri` only after the signed read has failed. A `from_node` reopen without the `"_rails"` fingerprint, or any other declaration under `on_load`, is a survey line rather than a drop.
causes.at_zero: the wire format is Rails' and the tolerant list is read off the reopen; the rule stays as a regression tripwire for either end drifting (a salt, digest, padding or `?expires_in` change fails the pinned literal first).

causes.title: Proving which address the HTTP client connects to — `TCPSocket.expects(:open).with { … }.throws`
causes.note: campfire's two DNS-rebinding tests stub `Resolv.getaddresses` with SEQUENTIAL answers (`.returns([a], [b])` — first call, then every later one), set `TCPSocket.expects(:open).with { |*args, **| … }` to `.never` for the hostname and `.throws(:dns_not_rebound)` for the resolved IP, and `assert_throws` around the fetch: the proof is which ADDRESS the client opened a socket to. Served since 2026-09-17: the Resolv slot files a sequence (`stub_getaddresses_seq`), `TcpSocketStub` (runtime/spinel/tcp_socket_stub.rb) holds the predicate expectations, and the client asks it about the address it is about to connect to — spinel's reopened `connect_with_timeout`, the ruby family's reopened `TCPSocket.open`. The `ipaddr:` pin itself had held on both lanes since matz/spinel#4420 closed; this is its proof.
causes.at_zero: served 2026-09-17 (sequential Resolv answers + the TcpSocketStub seam); the rule stays as a regression tripwire.

causes.title: `obj.extend Mod` on one live object
causes.note: Mixing a module into a single instance needs a per-object method table, which no compiled target has — spinel refuses the call at compile time, and one such line kept this whole file from linking. `lower::object_extend` now stubs the TEST that reaches for it with this report, so the file's other tests run. The test makes a `Room` attachable for one assertion; the honest answer is that the shape is dynamic.

causes.title: Global IDs — minting and dereferencing an sgid
causes.note: docs/pipeline/runtime.md now carries the split: `attachable_ids("User")` verifies an sgid and `lower::attachables_grep` rewrites `body.attachables.grep(User)` into a query over the ids, so a caller that NAMES its class resolves. The name-keyed dispatch exists now too: `ActionText::Attachable.locate` is generated per app as a `case` over the models that mix `Attachable` in, and `Attachment#attachable` resolves through it. What is left is MINTING — `to_gid_param` on a record — and a bare `attachables`, which still answers `[]` rather than the poly list the generated locator could now fill.

causes.title: `Rails.configuration` and the routes object
causes.match: (undefined method 'configuration' for module Rails|uninitialized constant Rails::Application::Routes)
causes.note: The emitted `Rails` module answers a small surface; the app reaches past it for configuration and for the application's route set (to build URLs outside a request). Each addition here is a decision about what part of Rails' global state the port models at all, rather than a missing method.

causes.title: `Turbo::StreamsChannel` as a constant the app can name
causes.note: Broadcasts lower to `Broadcasts.record`, which is the portable shape; the app also names the channel class directly to broadcast or to assert. The constant has no emitted counterpart, so those tests stop before reaching the broadcast at all.
causes.at_zero: the constant landed in fd1a3259; the rule stays as a regression tripwire.

causes.title: Broadcast assertions over a queue that is a log
causes.note: The emit records broadcasts into `Broadcasts.log` rather than delivering them through a cable adapter, so the app's own `assert_broadcasts` counts a different thing than it was written against. Ties into the cable work — the dispatch half, not the streaming half.

causes.title: A view helper called from a helper MODULE
causes.note: Inside a template these expand at transpile time. Inside a helper module the expansion has no template to splice into, so the call survives to runtime and lands on a bare module. Already the shape behind several closed findings (`button_to` with a block, `link_to` with a block); the remaining ones are the same wall a method away from the template.

causes.title: `belongs_to` autosave — an unsaved target saved with its owner
causes.note: Assigning an unsaved record and saving the owner saves the target first in Rails. The emit reads `value.id` (0) and the presence validation fails. Carries a stub entry in scripts/campfire-walk-stubs.rb, so the count here is what the stub does NOT cover.

causes.title: Active Storage — the attachment scopes and the bytes
causes.note: The metadata half answers (205c3031). What is left is the macro-generated preload scopes (`with_attached_*`, `with_rich_text_*`) and everything variant-shaped: `ActiveStorage::VariantWithRecord`, `representation` and `preview` on an `Attached`, and the bytes — the variants landed over ruby-vips and the video poster over ffmpeg (`Preview`), so a row here now is one of the preload scopes or a shape neither covers. Avatars and logos reach it now that the fixture-file helpers in front of them answer — clearing a wall ahead of this cause moves tests INTO it, which is what just happened.

causes.title: `fresh_when` / `stale?` — conditional GET
causes.note: ETag/Last-Modified handling on the controller. Small in surface and shared by every target once the response object carries the headers; the tests behind it assert 304s, so they are only reachable after it lands.
causes.at_zero: `fresh_when` / `stale?` landed in 7ea262e2; the rule stays as a regression tripwire.

causes.title: A route helper interpolated a record instead of its id
causes.note: `room_path(room)` rendered `#<Room:0x…>` into the path. Route helpers project to `.id` only where the SEGMENT holds one (8b4258e5); these are the sites that projection does not reach yet. Visible only as a wrong string, which is why they surface as redirect assertions rather than exceptions.

causes.title: A gem the emit does not carry
causes.note: web push, concurrent-ruby, and sentry-ruby. The RQRCode arm of this rule matches nothing now that qr_code_controller_test is green. Each is a decision about gem fate rather than modeling debt — shim the surface the app calls, or declare it out of scope and ledger it. None of them is on the path to more coverage than the tests naming it.

causes.title: geared_pagination's controller surface
causes.note: campfire paginates with geared_pagination — not pagy — whose concern injects `set_page_and_extract_portion_from` into the controller. It answers from a Base reopen in runtime/ruby/action_controller/pagination.rb, so the question underneath it (carry the gem, or lower pagination ourselves) was settled by lowering it.
causes.at_zero: landed in 0ef8fb79; the rule stays as a regression tripwire.

causes.title: An unsaved `id` is 0, not nil — and a lookup used it
causes.note: A deliberate divergence, ledgered in docs/pipeline/runtime.md: `ActiveRecord::Base#initialize` seeds `@id = 0` so ids stay plain machine integers across every target, where Rails answers nil. This is where that choice becomes visible — a code path that would have skipped a nil lookup instead performs one for id 0.
causes.at_zero: zero is the intended reading. This is a deliberate divergence rather than a gap, and the rule exists to catch the day it becomes visible again.

causes.title: An emitted method's arity does not match its caller
causes.note: The receiver exists and the name resolves; the shape does not. Usually a lowering that dropped or added a parameter — kwargs folded into a positional, a block-form helper emitted in its non-block shape. Each needs the emitted definition read against its call site.

causes.title: `allow_browser` — the modern-browser gate
causes.note: campfire's own concern calls `allow_browser versions: VERSIONS, block: -> { render template: "sessions/incompatible_browser" }`, so the version FLOOR is the app's (`{ safari: 17.2, chrome: 120, … }`) and what is missing is ours: the macro, its `block:` fallback, and parsing a User-Agent into a browser plus version. Rails reads that last part from the `useragent` gem's rule table — PORT the table, do not derive it. The file is 7/8 on this one test.

causes.title: A params hash interpolated into the request PATH
causes.note: The request went out as `POST /users/{params: {push_subscription: {…}}}` — the params object rendered into the path instead of being sent as the body. Bracket-nested query parameters are the shape behind it: the test writes `params: { push_subscription: { endpoint: …, keys: { … } } }` and nothing splits the nesting into a body. Reads as a routing error, which is why it sat untriaged.

causes.title: A table lock from the harness's shared-cache memory database
causes.note: SQLITE_LOCKED (6), not BUSY: the test database was SQLite's shared-cache memory URI, whose table locks never wait — a read cursor open on `accounts` on one connection makes an INSERT on another fail at once, `busy_timeout` notwithstanding. campfire's first-run race test (five threads posting the first account together) died on the lock before reaching the singleton guard it was written to prove: ~40% of runs on a Mac, one in eight on the box. Rails tests against a file (`storage/test.sqlite3`, `timeout: 5000`), so the harness does too now (test/test_helper.rb): writers wait, the guard answers.
causes.at_zero: the harness opens a per-test file database since 2026-09-17; the rule stays as the tripwire — a reappearance means a shim opened a shared-cache database again.

causes.title: Inline `render json:` reaches the CRuby-only encoder
causes.note: `render json: opengraph` lowered to `ActionController::JsonRender.encode(v)`, a reflective walk only the CRuby overlay defines — on the compiled lane the constant is unresolved and every `POST /unfurl_links` is a 500, so the app pasted links with no preview card. The key set is known at transpile time (the class's declared readers), so it is written down instead: an `as_json_str` writer on the class and `render plain: v.as_json_str, content_type: "application/json"` at the site (lower::as_json_poro). A value with no writer (a Hash literal, a Relation, a class with its own `as_json`) still reaches the encoder, and would still match here.
causes.at_zero: the monomorphized writer landed for the declared-readers case (campfire's only site); the rule stays as a regression tripwire, and names the shapes that would still reach the encoder.

causes.title: The emit ran and answered differently
causes.match: \A(assertion failed|assert_equal failed|assert_difference failed|assert_enqueued_jobs failed|not all expectations|expected |UNIQUE constraint)
causes.note: NOT a root cause — the bucket of tests that still need one. Nothing raised: the emitted code ran to completion and produced a different answer, so each of these has to be followed down its own chain. This is the most valuable cluster on the page and the most expensive: a missing method names itself, a wrong answer does not.
